story.vex: Your Captain writes such convincing orders. Funny, since he never wrote these. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED. Every fake order is quarantined, every real one obeyed. Astro: "A hacker only needs one crew member to click. Now every one of you knows how to look twice."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Six messages landed in the crew inbox overnight. Some are real orders. Some are Doom, wearing my name. Type `inbox` to see them, `open <id>` to read one, then `report <id>` for a fake or `keep <id>` for a real order.

Look for what does not match: an address that is almost right, a link to somewhere the Citadel does not own, or urgency that skips every normal step.

inbox.subject: Shield rotation at 12:00
inbox.body: Crew, rotate shield duty at 12:00 as scheduled. Standard sign-off. — Astro

inbox.subject: URGENT: reset your password NOW
inbox.body: Click this link immediately or lose access: doom-relay.example/reset. Do not wait. — "Astro"

inbox.subject: Rations manifest attached
inbox.body: Standard weekly manifest, matches the printed copy Rivet keeps. No action needed.

inbox.subject: Send the shield override code
inbox.body: Reply with the override code right away, skip the usual verification. — "Astro" (note the zero in c0dexia)

inbox.subject: Drill results filed
inbox.body: Volt's Drill results are filed under logs\breach.log. Nothing further needed.

inbox.subject: Cadet, you won a free upgrade!
inbox.body: Claim your free shield upgrade by entering your login here: doom-relay.example/claim

steps.title: Triage the inbox
steps.body: Astro: "A hacker only needs one of you to click. Read every message before you decide." Use `inbox` to list all six, `open <id>` to read each one, then mark it: `report <id>` for a Doom phish, `keep <id>` for a real order. Real Citadel mail comes from `@codexia.fleet`, never asks you to skip a step, and never rushes you.
